summary: Shigemitsu Dando studied at the University of Tokyo under Seiichiro Ono (~1932–1935). He held posts at the University of Tokyo (~1937–1974), Keio University (~1974–1983), and the Supreme Court of Japan (~1974–1983).

Kamata, working in Buddhist studies and Sinology, studied under Kodo Sawaki (~1947–1953) and at Komazawa University and the University of Tokyo. He held professorships at the University of Tokyo, Aichi Gakuin University, and the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies.
Shigeo Yokoyama, working in religious studies, studied at Kyoto University (~1974–1982). He held posts at Okayama University (~1991) and Nara Women's University.

Gorai, working in religious studies, Buddhist studies, and Japanology, studied at the University of Tokyo and Kyoto University. He held posts at Kyoto University of Education, Koyasan University, Otani University (1955–1978), and the Institute of Japanese Religious Folklore.
Shigeru Kato, a scholar of Sinology and history/archaeology, studied at the University of Tokyo from ~1903 to 1906. He later held an academic post at the University of Tokyo from ~1925 to 1941.

Shigeru Matsumoto, a religious studies scholar, studied at the University of Tokyo (~1953–1960) and Harvard University (~1960–1967). He held posts at Tenri University (~1967–1970) and the University of the Sacred Heart (~1970–2004).

Working in philosophy, Sinology, and Buddhist studies, Hu studied under Kaiten Nukariya and John Dewey at Cornell and Columbia. He served as chancellor of Peking University (1946–1948) and headed Academia Sinica (1957–1962), also holding a post at Fu Jen Catholic University.
Shih-Hsiang Chen, a Sinology scholar, studied at Peking University (~1932–1936). He later held a post at the University of California, Berkeley from ~1945 to 1971.
Shikazo Mori, a scholar in Sinology and history/archaeology, studied at Kyoto University (~1927–1930). He later held an academic post at Bukkyo University (~1970–1980).

Working in philosophy and Buddhist studies, Shili Xiong studied under Jian Ouyang at the China Institute of Inner Learning in 1920. He held posts at Boone University, Peking University (1923–1955), and Zhejiang University (~1942–1944).
Working in Iranian and Central Asian studies, linguistics, and Buddhist studies, Shimin Geng studied at Minzu University of China (~1949–1953) and subsequently held a post there from ~1953 to 2000.
Shin Fujinaga, a scholar in Indology and philosophy, held posts at the National Institute of Technology, Miyakonojo College (attested 1991 and 2000) and Hiroshima University (attested 1992).

Hisamatsu, a Buddhist studies and philosophy scholar, studied under Kitarō Nishida and Shozan Ikegami at Kyoto University. He served as professor at Hanazono University, Ryukoku University, Kyoto University (1935–1953), Kyoto City University of Arts, and visited Harvard University (1958).

Shin'ichi Yoshinaga, who worked in religious studies, Japanology, and Buddhist studies, studied at Kyoto University. He held a professorship at the National Institute of Technology, Maizuru College (attested 2015).

Shin'ya Yasutomi, a Buddhist studies scholar, studied at Waseda University and Otani University. He held multiple academic posts at Otani University, including professor (~1993–2010, 2014), and served as director of the Institute of Shin Buddhist Studies (~2005–2017).
Shindai Sekiguchi was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Taisho University (~1928–1934). He later served as a professor at Taisho University (~1956–1978) and at Hanazono University.

Takagi, a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar, studied at Tohoku University under Ensho Kanakura, Hakuyu Hadano, Gisho Nakano, and Yusho Miyasaka. He served at Koyasan University as associate professor (attested 1970) and later president (attested 1991–1995).

Shingo Einoo, an Indology, religious studies, and linguistics scholar, earned his PhD at the University of Marburg under Wilhelm Rau (~1979–1983). He held posts at the National Museum of Ethnology (~1983–1989) and the University of Tokyo (~1989–2013).

Shinichi Nakazawa, working in religious studies, Tibetology, and philosophy, studied at the University of Tokyo (~1969–1977). He held posts at Chuo University (~1993–2002), Tama Art University (~2002–2014), and Meiji University (~2011–2019).

Tsuda, in Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology, studied at the University of Tokyo under Akira Hirakawa and the Australian National University under J.W. de Jong and A.L. Basham. He held posts at the Eastern Institute and ICPBS.
